 MIA

 Davion Mitchell tallied 11 points (5-of-13 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), two rebounds, 10 assists, four steals and one block in Wednesday’s win over the Clippers.
 Mitchell’s start to the season has been better than most fantasy managers expected, with the Heat guard providing top-50 per-game value. He couldn’t buy a three-pointer on Wednesday, missing all five attempts, but Mitchell offered excellent production in assists and steals. And even with Wednesday’s poor shooting, Mitchell is still shooting 50 percent from the field this season. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Davion Mitchell

 Davion Mitchell finished with 15 points (5-of-5 FGs), seven assists, one block and four three-pointers on Monday against the Lakers. 
 While Mitchell had a spectacular game, volume was an issue. He didn’t miss a shot from the floor, but he only took five shots. Mitchell has had an excellent start to the year, but his lack of shot attempts prevented him from having a better night. However, he continues to dish out the dimes at a high rate, which has been the driving factor behind his top-75 value to start this season. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Davion Mitchell lit up the Mavericks with 21 points (9-of-15 FGs), two assists, three steals and two three-pointers on Monday. 
 It has been a fantastic start to the season for Mitchell, and that continued in this game. Through four games, he is averaging 18 points and seven assists per game while recording two double-doubles. He didn’t contribute as many dimes in this game, but his scoring has been consistent. He should continue to produce at a high level as Miami’s starting point guard. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Davion Mitchell led the Heat with 22 points (8-of-13 FGs), one rebound, 10 assists, one steal and three three-pointers in a 15-110 loss to the Hornets on Saturday. 
 Miami trailed by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, but Mitchell fueled a monster comeback, mostly with Giannis Antetokounmpo on the bench. That didn’t result in a win, but it was another strong performance for him. He has been fantastic this year, averaging 17.0 points, 8.7 assists and 2.3 three-pointers per game, all of which would be career bests for him. He has been a bright spot despite a rough start to the year for Miami. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Davion Mitchell produced 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 assists, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 The good news for fantasy managers was that Mitchell recorded a double-double, which included a game-high 10 assists. However, for category-league managers, the six turnovers hurt. Mitchell logged 33 minutes in Wednesday’s opener, with Pelle Larsson (two points, three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block) taking on the playmaking responsibilities when “Off Night” was on the bench. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo can also initiate the offense, and they’ll likely need to because Miami lacks depth at point guard. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 BKN 
 Forward 
 #17 
 Davion Mitchell had 13 Points, (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, two steals and a 3-pointer on Wednesday. 
 Davion showed how much of a pest he is defensively in this game with his full court pressure and defensive numbers. He did leave the game temporarily after hitting his head on Day’Ron Sharpe’s knee, but he returned to the game. He should be primed to at worst, be a steals and assists streamer for redraft leagues. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #2 
 Davion Mitchell notched three points (1-of-5 FGs), one rebound, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s exhibition against the Raptors. 
 Like the other Heat starters, Mitchell was shut down at the half. He didn’t have a great night shooting, but that shouldn’t dissuade fantasy managers from selecting “Off Night” in drafts. Miami lacks depth at point guard, especially with Dru Smith (hamstring) not guaranteed to be fully ready when the regular season begins. With Giannis Antetokounmpo joining the lineup, Mitchell could potentially provide more value in assists and three-pointers than he did in 2025-26. 
 Dru Smith 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #12 
 According to Ira Winderman of the Sun-Sentinel, Dru Smith (calf) is out for “a couple of weeks.” 
 Smith, who played a career-high 70 games last season, is dealing with a strained right calf. With the reported timeline, he may be limited when the regular season begins. Smith’s absence doesn’t affect fantasy basketball, but it does leave a Heat team already light on options at point guard down a rotation piece. Starter Davion Mitchell has become more important, especially if Smith isn’t ready when the regular season begins. 
 Kasparas Jakučionis 
 MIL 
 Guard 
 The Athletic’s Sam Amick reports the Bucks pushed for Kasparas Jakučionis to be included in the trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo. 
 Amick, citing league sources, reports the Heat initially attempted to include Davion Mitchell in the trade rather than Jakučionis. With Mitchell on an expiring contract, the Bucks wanted a player with more time remaining on their rookie contract. It was a reasonable ask considering two of the other players the Bucks acquired (Tyler Herro and Jaimie Jaquez Jr.) are also on expiring deals. The Bucks held out and landed Jakučionis, who has three years left on his contract. He remains an intriguing dynasty asset on the rebuilding Bucks. 
 Davion Mitchell 
 MIA 
 Guard 
 #45 
 Davion Mitchell amassed 28 points (12-of-24 FGs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets. 
 Mitchell logged a game-high 48 minutes on Tuesday and did just about everything the Heat could have hoped for. He shot the ball well en route to leading the team in scoring, was one of Miami’s top facilitators, and was the Heat’s only player with at least one block and steal apiece. Unfortunately for Mitchell, his blocked game-winning layup attempt will be the lasting memory of what was a very strong performance. Mitchell played 70 games this season and made a big step as a passer. Yet he wasn’t a reliable option when it came to fantasy basketball. 
 Andrew Wiggins 
 MIA 
 Forward 
 #22 
 Andrew Wiggins totaled 27 points (10-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, three assists and four three-pointers in the loss to the Hornets on Friday. 
 Wiggins was one of several Heat players to make positive contributions on the offensive end of the floor. His 27 points trailed only Davion Mitchell’s 28, as the veteran forward had production across all three scoring levels. Wiggins was also one of the Heat’s best rebounders on the night during his 42 minutes of game action. He finished the season as a fairly comparable fantasy basketball performer as he was a season ago, albeit on fewer points per game. If Wiggins remains on the Heat going forward, he could be in for a similar season.

 Devin Booker led the Suns with 30 points (11-of-22 FGs), one rebound, eight assists, three steals and four three-pointers in a 117-104 win over the Magic on Thursday.
 Booker has had a few rough performances early on this season, but this has been an excellent two-game stretch for him. He has scored at least 30 points in back-to-back games, and he set a new season high for assists, steals and three-pointers in this one. Outside of a dud game against the Thunder, Booker has been excellent this season. He’ll continue to have the ball in his hands, and if he’s shooting the ball this well, the results will continue to be great for fantasy managers.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Miles Bridges 
 PHX 
 Forward 
 #22 
 Player Stats

 Miles Bridges stuffed the stat sheet on Thursday with 18 points (6-of-10 FGs), 13 rebounds, five assists, two steals and three three-pointers against the Magic.
 With both Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach in foul trouble, Bridges was able to step up on the glass. He ended up setting a new season high for rebounds in what has been an excellent start to the year for him, especially as of late. Over his last four games, Bridges has averaged 20.3 points, 9.0 rebounds, 3.8 assists, 2.3 steals, 1.0 block and 3.0 triples per game while shooting 51.8 percent from the free throw line. He has been fantastic in fantasy basketball and will look to stay hot against the Rockets on Saturday.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Dillon Brooks posted a full line on Thursday with 24 points (9-of-16 FGs), one rebound, one assist, two steals, one block and four three-pointers against the Magic.
 Brooks’ scoring has dropped off this season, but he has made up for it with improved efficiency. However, he was able to do both in this game, which led to his best scoring performance of the season. Brooks has shot at least 55 percent from the floor in three of his last four games, which has helped his value in nine-category leagues. He likely won’t continue to shoot this well, but he certainly has the hot hand right now.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Oso Ighodaro started on Thursday and finished with two points (1-of-2 FGs), five rebounds, one assist and one block against the Magic.
 Head coach Jordan Ott made the call to replace Khaman Maluach with Ighodaro in the starting unit. Unfortunately, Ighodaro found himself in foul trouble throughout the game, which prevented him from providing much value. Ighodaro is worth considering as a waiver wire pickup, even if this first game as a starter was rough. He won’t do much scoring, but he’s a strong passer for a big man and has five blocks over his last three games.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Tristan da Silva provided a boost off the bench with 18 points (6-of-15 FGs), two rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.
 All season long, da Silva has been a solid source of offense off the bench for Orlando, and he was able to provide that once again in this game. Unfortunately, he hasn’t been able to provide much outside of points and three-pointers, outside of a singular double-digit rebounding game last week. Aside from that night, da Silva hasn’t had more than four rebounds in a game. He’ll continue to score, but noting else will come consistently.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Wendell Carter Jr. led the Magic with 27 points (10-of-12 FGs), 13 rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers against the Suns on Thursday.
 Carter has had a few 20-point games this season and a few 10-rebound games, but he hadn’t done both at the same time until this game. He also set new season highs for both categories in what ended up being his best performance of the season. WCJ has been excellent to start the year, though he has had a four poor games mixed in. In all likelihood, WCJ will continue to provide inconsistent value, with a combination of big games and duds mixed in.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Franz Wagner 
 ORL

 Franz Wagner recorded a double-double on Thursday with 15 points (7-of-13 FGs, 1-of-4 FTs), eight rebounds, 15 assists, four steals and six turnovers in a 117-104 loss to the Suns.
 With both Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) out, Wagner has stepped up as the team’s primary playmaker. That has led to some incredible assist numbers this season. He matched his previous career high for dimes last week before setting it last weekend. He set a new career high for assists once again in this game. Wagner has taken on a lot of responsibility on both ends of the floor, but he hasn’t excelled as a scorer. Still, he has been productive in other categories while trying to keep Orlando afloat until they get healthier.
 -  Noah Rubin
